projection.description: Concept projection. Every relation label is defined once in relationCatalogue with its family, class, transitivity, impact direction and inverse. Inverses are derived, not stored.

Structural.description: What a thing is made of or what kind of thing it is. Part-whole and subtype relationships only.

classes.decomposition: Part-whole: the source is the whole and the target is one of its parts. Transitive.
classes.classification: Subtype: the source is a kind of the target. Transitive. Kept separate from part-whole because the two do not compose.

Structural.graphUse: Use for decomposition trees, C4 containment, DMBOK knowledge areas and type hierarchies.

Behavioural.description: What things do at run time or in operation: who depends on whom, what flows where, and who performs which activity.

classes.dependency: The source needs the target to work. A change to the target can impact the source.
classes.flow: Data, artefacts, information or value pass from one end to the other, or the source produces the target.
classes.activity: An actor, team or practice (source) performs or looks after an activity or thing (target).

Behavioural.graphUse: Use for dependency analysis, data and value flow, pipelines and operating responsibilities.

Causal.description: Cause and effect. Every edge points from cause to effect, so a directed walk is a consequence chain and a reverse walk is root-cause analysis.

classes.propagation: A state or event at the source makes a harmful effect at the target happen or more likely.
classes.mitigation: The source removes or reduces an effect, risk or harm at the target.
classes.enablement: The source makes a beneficial effect at the target happen or more likely.

Causal.graphUse: Use for incident, risk, SLO, outcome, control and model-drift reasoning.

Temporal.description: Order and validity in time: what happens before what, what triggers what, lifecycle state changes, versions and effective dates.

classes.sequence: The source happens before, or starts, the target.
classes.lifecycle: The source moves to a new lifecycle state, represented by the target.
classes.versioning: The target is a dated revision of the source.
classes.validity: The target is the date that bounds when the source applies.

Temporal.graphUse: Use for lifecycle sequences, release paths, model promotion and policy or control validity.

Governance.description: Authority, accountability and measurement: who owns what, which rules apply, and how performance is measured.

classes.governance: The source sets, applies or enforces rules, constraints or direction for the target.
classes.ownership: Accountability or assignment between a party and what it is accountable for.
classes.measurement: The source measures, monitors, targets or costs the target.

Governance.graphUse: Use for policy-to-control chains, ownership, stewardship, access control, audit and measurement views.

Semantic.description: Meaning across layers: what realises what, what represents or describes what, and what is aligned with what.

classes.realisation: A more concrete element (or the source, for active labels) realises a more abstract one.
classes.representation: The source describes, records, maps or derives from the target. It is information about something, not the thing itself.
classes.alignment: The source is aimed at or consistent with the target, without dependency or cause.

Semantic.graphUse: Use for cross-layer traceability (business to application to technology), metadata and GraphRAG expansion.

accelerates.definition: The source helps the target learn or deliver faster.

accountable for.definition: The source answers for the target's results or quality.

achieves.definition: The source brings the target result about.

acts on.definition: The source takes automated action against the target.

adapts.definition: The source tailors its rules into the target.

addresses.definition: The source is aimed at the target.

administers.definition: The source runs and supports the target.

adopts.definition: The source takes up the target way of working.

affects.definition: The source changes the target's state or exposure.

calls for.definition: The source obliges the target to be carried out.

can affect.definition: A change or failure at the source can change the target.

can cause.definition: The source can bring about the target.

can precede.definition: The source may happen before the target.

catalogued in.definition: A record of the source is published in the target.

causes.definition: The source brings about the target.

charters.definition: The source formally sets up the target and its mandate.

composed of.definition: The source is built from the target.

comprises.definition: The source is made up of the target, among other parts.

conducts.definition: The source carries out the target activity.

configures.definition: The source sets up the target.

constructs.definition: The source builds the target model or structure.

consumes.definition: The source reads or takes in what the target provides.

contains.definition: The target is a part held inside the source.

contributes to.definition: The source moves the target measure.

controls.definition: The source holds authority over the target.

creates.definition: The source brings the target benefit about.

curates.definition: The source selects, organises and looks after the target's content.

defines.definition: The source sets out the target.

degrades.definition: The source lowers the target's performance or quality.

delivered via.definition: The source reaches its consumers through the target.

delivers.definition: The source hands the target over to its consumers.

deployed as.definition: The source becomes the running target once deployed.

deploys.definition: The source installs software into the target.

derives from.definition: The source is derived from the target.

describes.definition: The source is information about the target.

designs.definition: The source produces the design of the target.

detects.definition: The source observes that the target has occurred.

develops.definition: The source carries out the target practice.

drives.definition: The source is a reason the target happens or changes.

effective from.definition: The source applies from the target date.

emits.definition: The source publishes the target when something happens.

enables.definition: The source makes the target possible.

enforced by.definition: The source is made effective by the target.

enforces.definition: The source makes sure the target is followed.

engineers.definition: The source designs and builds for the target quality.

ensures.definition: The source is accountable for the target being met.

establishes.definition: The source creates and approves the target.

executes.definition: The source runs the target activity.

exposed via.definition: The source is offered to consumers through the target.

exposes.definition: The source makes its behaviour available through the target.

facilitates.definition: The source makes the target easier to do.

feeds.definition: Data or artefacts flow from the source into the target.

fits in.definition: The source sits within the target's scope.

generates.definition: The source emits the target as a by-product of running.

governed by.definition: The source must follow the rules set by the target.

governs.definition: The source sets the rules the target must follow.

grants.definition: The source is given the target permission.

guides.definition: The source sets direction for the target.

has.definition: The target is a part or attribute of the source.

has lineage.definition: The target records where the source came from and how it changed.

has version.definition: The target is a dated revision of the source.

hosted on.definition: The source runs on the target.

identifies.definition: The source discovers and records the target.

implemented by.definition: The source is put into effect by the target.

implements.definition: The source puts the target into effect.

includes.definition: The target is a member or part of the source.

increases.definition: The source raises the level of the target.

incurs.definition: The source gives rise to the target spend.

informs.definition: Information from the source is an input to the target's decisions or design.

ingests.definition: The source collects data from the target.

input for.definition: The source is an input that the target processes.

integrates.definition: The source carries out the target integration.

integrates with.definition: The source exchanges data or calls with the target across a boundary.

interacts with.definition: The source uses or communicates with the target.

is type of.definition: The source is a subtype or kind of the target and inherits its meaning.

led by.definition: The source is led by the target.

leverages.definition: The source draws on the target's outputs to do its work.

maintains.definition: The source keeps the target current and correct.

manages.definition: The source looks after the target day to day.

mandates.definition: The source requires the target to be in place.

manipulates.definition: The source creates, reads, updates or deletes the target.

maps.definition: The source shows the target and its relationships.

maps to.definition: The source corresponds to the target in another model or layer.

may trigger.definition: The source can start the target.

measured by.definition: The source is quantified by the target.

mitigates.definition: The source lowers the likelihood or impact of the target.

monitors.definition: The source watches the target continuously.

offers.definition: The source makes the target available to others.

operates on.definition: The source reads or changes the target as part of its behaviour.

operationalised by.definition: The source is put into practice through the target.

optimises.definition: The source improves the target's cost or performance.

orchestrates.definition: The source co-ordinates the target's activities.

owns.definition: The source is accountable for the target.

packages.definition: The source bundles software into the target for deployment.

partitioned into.definition: The source is divided into non-overlapping parts, one of which is the target.

performed by.definition: The source activity or ability is carried out by the target.

performs.definition: The source carries out the target activity.

persists.definition: The source stores and retrieves the target.

populates.definition: The source fills the target with content.

precedes.definition: The source happens before the target.

produces.definition: The source creates the target as an output.

promotes to.definition: The source moves to the target lifecycle state.

proposes.definition: The source puts the target forward for decision.

protects.definition: The source shields the target from outside influence.

provides.definition: The source offers or runs the target for others.

raises.definition: The source opens the target, for example from an alert.

realised as.definition: The source is made real as the target.

realised by.definition: The source is made real by the more concrete target.

recommends.definition: The source advises that the target be put in place or changed.

reduces.definition: The source lowers the level of the target.

registered in.definition: A record of the source is held in the target.

registers.definition: The source holds the record of the target.

releases.definition: The source makes the target available to users.

relieves.definition: The source removes or reduces the target pain.

represented by.definition: The source is stood for by the target.

represents.definition: The source stands for the target in another layer.

requires.definition: The source cannot work or be achieved without the target.

restricted by.definition: Access to or use of the source is limited by the target.

seeks.definition: The source wants to obtain the target.

served by.definition: The source is provided by the target at run time.

serves.definition: The source delivers value to the target.

specifies.definition: The source writes the specification of the target.

standardises.definition: The source sets the standard form of the target.

supports.definition: The source helps the target do its work.

synthesises.definition: The source is combined and distilled into the target.

targets.definition: The source sets a target level for the target.

traces.definition: The source records the origin and movement of the target.

tracks.definition: The source follows the target over time.

unit cost for.definition: The source expresses spend per unit of the target.

uses.definition: The source relies on the target to do its work.

Causal: What downstream operational, customer or regulatory consequences could this event trigger?
Which risks increase if this service degrades?

Which policy or control versions are effective at a given point in time?
What lifecycle activities follow this incident?
What sequence leads from discovery to deployment and monitoring?
